html:
SMTO-GWT-0042 — Part of this computer's Gateway installation is missing or broken

GUID: cea30547-7301-499d-a267-0624fd2cda39
Slug: gateway-runtime-installation-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • When the Gateway on this computer was installed or checked, one of its required parts failed its test. Features that need that part, such as the web browser, documents or charts, may not work there until it is repaired.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Before repairing, make sure no Task is still running on that computer. Let it finish or stop it. The installer may restart the Gateway, which would interrupt work still running there.
  2. On that computer, run the Gateway installer again, signed in as the same user account that normally runs the Gateway. The parts must work for the account that runs the Gateway, not just for whoever installed it.
  3. Read the installer's messages for lines starting with MISSING/BROKEN, install the program they name (for example git, tesseract or docker), then run the installer once more. Each of those lines names the exact part that failed its check.
  4. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that computer. This confirms SMTO can reach the repaired Gateway before you send it work.

What success looks like

  • The installer finishes without MISSING/BROKEN lines, and the computer shows Connected in the Gateways list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, together with the installer's MISSING/BROKEN lines, to the person who manages that computer. Don't delete the Gateway's data folder or turn off security checks to make it look healthy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway installation or readiness check failed: a dependency version or the full installation profile, a Python import, bundled skill registration, a local smoke test (manual rendering, Matplotlib, office/pdf/ocr), a native tool, or the Chromium launch check; the caught failure alone does not prove an editable-install cause.

What this means

  • Installation or readiness checks failed a dependency version, installed-package location, feature registration or functional smoke test. A caught exception does not establish that an editable install is the specific cause. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Installation or readiness checks failed a dependency version, installed-package location, feature registration or functional smoke test. A caught exception does not establish that an editable install is the specific cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the named dependency or smoke-test failure and effective installation path; distinguish missing software from an incompatible version or a failed native launch/render.

How to fix it

  • Read the MISSING/BROKEN lines printed by gateway_core.installation_check (or the 'Gateway browser setup failed' message from gateway_core/browser/install_check.py) to find the failed check. Repair that prerequisite and rerun the Gateway installer (src/gateway_agent/install.sh or the release installer) under the Gateway's actual OS account; finish or stop active work on that Gateway before any restart the installer performs.
  • Repair the specific failed prerequisite using the supported installer on that host. Reconcile active work before a required restart.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The affected installation check and the Gateway's readiness check pass under its actual OS account.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
